newsitem.title: USA: U.S. GRAIN DEALERS TAKING 15-20 PROTECTION ON SOY.
newsitem.headline: U.S. GRAIN DEALERS TAKING 15-20 PROTECTION ON SOY.

text.p: In anticipation of a sharply lower CBOT open and reports of grain movement early Monday, U.S. Midwest merchandisers were taking up to 20 cents per bushel cash protection on soybeans and up to 10 cents on corn.
"There's got to be a lot of grain moving this morning," said one Mississippi River dealer.
The early sales and lower CBOT calls were spurred by widespread rains across dry areas of the Corn Belt on Sunday and Monday, dealers said.
"Peoria got two inches of rain, and they needed it," one dealer said.
CBOT soybeans were expected to open 10 to 15 cents per bushel lower, corn was seen three to five lower, and wheat was expected to open one to two cents lower.
